globalPass: The asset has a named product job and exact destination before import or creation.
The source file, provenance and status are recorded in the manifest or registry.
The real app data source is canonical; visual concepts never define membership or unlock state.
Private mission or badge meaning remains PIN/private-safe on every public-capable surface.
The asset is legible at actual iPhone render size and has useful accessible text.
Wiring, missing-file, duplicate-ID and privacy regressions pass before deployment.
globalReject: A pretty asset with no trigger, destination or product job
A badge that merely duplicates a mission level or another badge
A new visual pack while approved live art already fills the same job
Private wording or identity leaking into a public/exportable route
A broad theme migration approved only from a mockup
Any generation or credit spend launched from this read-only hub
badgePass: One stable ID maps to one original asset and one exact unlock condition.
The badge communicates an achievement that is meaningfully different from daily character growth.
Unlock is derived from persisted canonical state and can be reproduced in a test.
The Trophy Case placement, unlock moment and optional Home feature obey their separate density rules.
badgeReject: The art cannot be matched to a unique achievement
It relies on fake or manually implied progress
It needs a separate generated locked-state image
It clutters Home or competes with Daily Missions 2.0

themeDirection.name: Warm White + Oxblood
rules: White stays dominant; red creates hierarchy, not a permanent alarm state.
Use oxblood for anchors and active states, bright red only for small moments.
Keep success green and warnings amber so red retains brand meaning.
Validate in Lab and on an installed iPhone before migrating shared app tokens.
